issues.title: HTTPS links with and without :443 should not be duplicated
issues.body: An old report: exporting https://example.com:443/docs and https://example.com/docs creates two entries. Investigate whether this is already addressed on main before implementing another fix.

issues.title: Signed URLs lose meaning if query parameters are discarded
issues.body: The query string can contain signatures, repeated keys, tracking-looking keys or routing state. Add explicit regression coverage proving names, values, order and repetitions are preserved by normalization and all exports.

issues.title: Expose CSV output from the command line
issues.body: Add --format csv to the CLI using the library exporter. Related library work is required; default JSON behavior must remain compatible.

issues.title: Add CSV export for spreadsheet users
issues.body: Add a CSV exporter with a url header, stable first-seen deduplication, shared URL normalization and correct quoting. Keep this library change separate from CLI wiring.

issues.title: Collapse saved links that only differ after the hash
issues.body: Saving https://example.com/guide#a and https://example.com/guide#b produces two entries. Need an optional way to save one document entry rather than each section. Existing defaults must stay compatible.

issues.title: Bookmarks with different section anchors appear twice
issues.body: JSON export currently treats https://example.com/guide#intro and https://example.com/guide#install as different bookmarks. Add opt-in fragment-free identity while keeping current behavior the default. Shared normalizer, export and CLI should agree.

pull_requests.title: fix: canonicalize default HTTP and HTTPS ports
pull_requests.description: Closes #1. Fix URL identity in the shared normalizer; JSON export and CLI inherit the same behavior. Preserve nondefault ports, path, query and fragment. Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v — 6 tests passed, including IPv6 and nondefault-port regression coverage.

generated_descriptions.short_why: The URL normalizer was treating default HTTP and HTTPS ports as part of the URL identity, which could lead to inconsistent canonicalization and duplicate-equivalent URLs. This fix addresses issue #1 and ensures default ports are normalized away while preserving meaningful URL parts like nondefault ports, path, query, and fragment.
generated_descriptions.short_how: Updated the shared URL normalizer so HTTP/HTTPS default ports are canonicalized consistently. The behavior now applies across JSON export and the CLI, and regression tests were added/updated to cover IPv6 and nondefault-port cases.
generated_descriptions.long: Closes #1. Fix URL identity in the shared normalizer; JSON export and CLI inherit the same behavior. Preserve nondefault ports, path, query and fragment. Checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v — 6 tests passed, including IPv6 and nondefault-port regression coverage.

change.title: feat: export bookmarks to spreadsheet CSV
change.body: Closes #5. CSV library output with a url header, standard-library quoting, shared normalization and stable deduplication. Checks: 7 tests passed. CLI wiring is a separate change.
change.author: gvago

diff.patch:
@@ -6,3 +6,15 @@ from bookmarks.urls import normalize_url
 def export_json(urls: list[str]) -> str:
     """Export unique normalized URLs in first-seen order."""
     return json.dumps(list(dict.fromkeys(normalize_url(url) for url in urls)), indent=2)
+
+
+def export_csv(urls: list[str]) -> str:
+    """Export normalized unique URLs as one CSV column."""
+    import csv
+    import io
+
+    output = io.StringIO(newline="")
+    writer = csv.writer(output)
+    writer.writerow(["url"])
+    writer.writerows([url] for url in dict.fromkeys(normalize_url(url) for url in urls))
+    return output.getvalue()

@@ -25,6 +25,13 @@ class URLTests(unittest.TestCase):
 
 
 class ExportTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_csv_export(self):
+        import csv
+        import io
+        from bookmarks.exports import export_csv
+        rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(export_csv(["HTTPS://Example.com/a?x=1,2", "https://example.com/a?x=1,2"]))))
+        self.assertEqual(rows, [["url"], ["https://example.com/a?x=1,2"]])
+
     def test_export_reuses_url_identity(self):
         import json
         from bookmarks.exports import export_json

     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Normalize and deduplicate bookmarks as JSON")
     parser.add_argument("urls", nargs="+")

+        if args.format == "csv":
+            sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="")
+        print(output, end="" if output.endswith("\n") else "\n")

+        import io
+        import subprocess
+        import sys
